summary_paraphrase: Khuzwayo loves to dance and is chosen to perform the Ingoma harvest dance. Afraid of dancing before people from many villages, he says he cannot do it and runs off. The village searches; his two best friends find him in the maize field. He tells them he is nervous of making a mistake, and they practise with him until he feels ready. On the day he leads his village to the arena, a little nervous still, and his dance is loved by all.

notes: OBSERVED: where he runs to is never said; a wordless full-bleed spread (page 6) shows the friends finding him in the maize field.

OBSERVED: scale carries feeling: tiny alone on a white spread when worried (page 3), small among cut-off giant legs when practising with the older dancers (page 10), large and central when dancing (page 12).
OBSERVED: typography acts: on page 4 the words step down and grow like footsteps as he leaves the right edge; on page 12 the lines grow larger toward the payoff.
OBSERVED: the comfort of friends is physical and pictured only (arm round shoulders, hand on arm, pages 7-8).
OBSERVED: the closing vignette (not counted as a story page) shows him dancing alone in his everyday clothes, the same pose as page 1: the book closes on the opening image.
OBSERVED: the cover shows him already in the Ingoma costume, so the reader knows the ending before page 1.

strengths: fear is named in the child's own words and answered by peers, not by an adult
a wordless reveal spread at the centre of the book
the fear is reduced, not erased: still a little nervous on the day
picture scale tracks how big or small he feels
a culturally specific occasion explained in one sentence
weaknesses: the solution is told in a line (grows more confident) rather than shown through an attempt or setback
the dance itself is over in one spread; the climax is brief
the two friends have no names or voices of their own beyond helping
longest sentence 18 words on the procession page

anti_patterns.note: one practice session and a statement of growing confidence carry him from fleeing to ready; no failed attempt

age_suitability.notes: A stage-fright story resolved by friends. Peak fear 4 of 5 on page 4 (says it is too scary and runs off), about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale; the closing payoff is joy 5 of 5, about 3 on the 0-3 scale. The child runs off alone and cannot be found for a while; this is shown as fear, not praised, and is resolved by friends without danger, so no content flag. Ingoma is presented respectfully by South African creators. Mean sentence 6.9 words, longest 18; theme (performance nerves, being chosen) fits 5-6. Where he hides and the friends' comfort live only in pictures (MagicPaper stories are text-only today).
